questions.question: Which items should this "Memory driver is bug-free and a solid template" work cover?

options.label: 4 core items (Recommended)
options.description: BUG-328, BK-441, BK-442, BK-440 in one PR. Each is effort S, and each is a flaw in Memory, in the driver API every backend inherits, or in the formal model. Glob, mutation and docs items stay separate.

options.label: Core + the glob bugs
options.description: Also BUG-298 (glob anchored with `$` also matches a key ending in a newline) and BK-405 (ext.glob gives different answers for non-canonical patterns). These sit in shared glob code, not the driver; the PR touches more backends and its review takes longer.

options.label: Core + a driver.py docs item
options.description: Also file a new item to make the driver protocol state what a hierarchical driver with implicit parents must provide (the trace marked it 'unclear'), so the template documents itself.

options.label: Everything listed
options.description: Core, the glob bugs, BK-407 (mutation scopes) and BK-339 (behavior matrix, size M). The broadest scope, and the slowest to converge.

questions.question: BUG-328: writing a `bytearray` or `memoryview` to Memory fails with a misleading AlreadyExists/InvalidPath. Which fix?

options.label: Accept buffer types (Recommended)
options.description: Add bytearray and memoryview to `WritableContent`; both drivers store `bytes(content)`. The kernel already passes them through, and any later driver would have to handle them too.

options.label: Refuse them with a typed error
options.description: Keep `WritableContent` as it is and raise a clear TypeError/InvalidArgument when the kernel receives one, so no driver ever sees one.

questions.question: BK-441: a driver that leaves out a required method inherits its empty body, so for example an omitted `delete` reports success. What should happen?

options.label: Refuse at construction (Recommended)
options.description: DriverBackend raises when it is built if a required method is still the protocol's empty body (`probe` excepted). Fails closed, matching how missing optional protocols are already refused.

options.label: Warn at construction
options.description: Emit a warning and keep going. Lenient for half-finished drivers, but the silent no-op stays possible.

questions.question: BK-442: `from remote_store.drivers import Driver` loads the whole async package and its cloud SDKs. Which fix?

options.label: Lazy module __getattr__ (Recommended)
options.description: `AsyncDriverBackend` and the other async names load on first use, with a `__dir__` so dir() and pydoc still list them. Same pattern as `remote_store.aio` for the Memory classes; the import path stays the same.

options.label: Split the module
options.description: Sync names stay in `remote_store.drivers`; async names move to e.g. `remote_store.aio.drivers`. Cleaner separation, but it changes an import path published yesterday, so it needs a migration note.

questions.question: BK-440: the Dafny `Write` checks WR-010's metadata gate after the folder/ancestor/AlreadyExists checks; the kernel checks it first. How should the model change?

options.label: Reorder, gate first (Recommended)
options.description: Move the WR-010 clause right after BE-029's root clause and guard the IsDir, ancestor and AlreadyExists clauses with `!(metadata gate fires)`. The model then proves the order every driver inherits, and the stale 'ordering divergence' comment goes. Re-verify via Docker Dafny; the compiled oracle may need regenerating.

options.label: Carve out the three states
options.description: Leave the order alone and exclude metadata-without-capability inputs from the three clauses. Less churn, but the model then says nothing about what the kernel answers there.

BUG-328, revised: widening the public `WritableContent` would bind every backend that isn't on the kernel yet. Which fix?

options.label: Fix the drivers, keep the public type (Recommended)
options.description: Both Memory drivers accept every type the kernel hands them, as `bytes(content)`. A test checks a driver honours the protocol's whole `Content` type, which future drivers then follow. Public `WritableContent` stays `bytes | BinaryIO`; a later item can widen it.

options.label: Widen the public type everywhere
options.description: `WritableContent` gains bytearray and memoryview; Store, Local, S3, SFTP, Azure, SQLBlob, HTTP and the cache/observe wrappers all accept them, with conformance cells. Effort M to L, and it grows this PR's review across every backend.

options.label: Refuse with a typed error in the kernel
options.description: The kernel raises a clear TypeError for bytearray/memoryview and narrows `_io.Content` to `bytes | BinaryIO`. Consistent with the public type, but it takes away a capability the kernel already has.

questions.question: BUG-328, corrected: the driver protocol's `Content` type is `bytes | BinaryIO`, and the kernel passes buffers through without the type saying so. Where should the fix go?

options.label: Kernel converts to bytes (Recommended)
options.description: The kernel's write entry points turn a bytearray or memoryview into `bytes` before any driver sees it, so drivers only ever get what the protocol types say. Every future driver is covered without code. Public `WritableContent` unchanged; costs one copy of a buffer, which Memory makes anyway.

options.label: Widen the protocol type
options.description: `Content` (and the driver `put` signature) gains bytearray | memoryview, and both Memory drivers handle them. Every later driver author must then handle buffers too, which is more surface for each S3/Azure/SFTP driver.

options.description: `guard_content` raises TypeError before any I/O for content with no `read` (sync) or `__aiter__` (async), and the marked stream raises a caller-marked TypeError when a read returns non-bytes, so it passes through verbatim. Every driver gets it; covered under BUG-328's entry with cells on both runtimes.
